newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to provide details of D.C. renewal plan.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to provide details of D.C. renewal plan.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday afternoon will provide further details about a proposed $285 million private-public corporation to revitalize the District of Columbia, the White House said.
The announcement is scheduled for 1625 EST (2125 GMT).

The president will recommend that the proposed Economic Development Corporation receive about $235 million in U.S. tax breaks and a direct federal contribution of about $50 million, a knowledgeable source told Reuters.
The White House previously said that employers could use the tax credits to hire low and moderate-income workers in distressed parts of the city.

At the White House media briefing on Tuesday, Clinton is expected to propose that D.C. employers receive a 40 percent tax credit for the first $10,000 in eligible wages paid to the low-income workers they hire, the source said.
The White House also has said that the new corporation could leverage the direct federal dollars through the issuance of tax-exempt bonds.
It is unclear how much of the $50 million in direct contributions could be used for that purpose, the source said.
The $235 million tax-incentive program would build on the administration's empowerment zone and enterprise community program, the president is expected to say.

The proposed economic development corporation is part of a broad $3.9 billion, five-year revitalization plan for the city announced by Clinton earlier this year. The administration is expected to send a final plan to Congress in the next two weeks.
